newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk stock mkt watching preliminary motion debate.
newsitem.headline: Turk stock mkt watching preliminary motion debate.

text.p: Istanbul shares kept most of the morning gains on Tuesday afternoon as the market began to follow a preliminary debate in parliament on a censure motion against the Islamist-led coalition government, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 which ended the morning session 0.8 percent higher at 1,504, stood at 1,500 at 1232 GMT, up 0.67 percent from Friday. The market was closed for holiday on Monday.

Brokers said news that the small far-right Islamist party BBP pledged support for the government in today's preliminary vote prompted sales in early afternoon, causing the index to fall from a high of 1,518.
"The BBP statement produced worries that the coalition may survive the vote. But I expect buying towards the close," said Hasan Soydan from Garanti securities.

The decision of the BBP which has seven deputies could swing the tight vote in favour of the Islamist-led alliance which has 280 deputies in the 550-seat parliament. The opposition has said they had some support from the coalition's conservative wing.

A simple majority of those in parliament are needed for the motion to go forward to a full debate on Thursday and a further no-confidence vote on Saturday. But Turkish political tradition dictates a government resign if it loses the first round.
The government has been losing blood heavily since the secularist military began pushing it in February to stamp out rising Islamist activism.
